So I had to just overspend a little bit" (t=2190) and "The Ebarb stayed alive" (t=2227).

bullets: CRL 2026 World Finals duel vs Sandbox (bridge spam), video t=1943.9-2250.1. Ryley calls it "this rocket cycle deck" and states the plan up front — "I just felt like any matchup I trust my defense, I can win" (t=1953-1957). Result: loss.

The list runs Evo Cannon and Evo Princess, and the Berserker slot is the Hero variant: he uses Savage Survival twice, both times on defence against a Giant Skeleton (t=2170, t=2211), never for tower damage.

Piloting pattern: Cannon is the spine and is cycled back constantly (t=1962.5, 2038, 2062, 2093, 2216) with Ice Spirit, Skeletons, Berserker and The Log layered on top; the peak of it is t=2093-2110, holding an evolved Battle Ram and a Giant Skeleton in opposite lanes for zero tower damage — "Was taking absolutely no damage, but I was down five elixir" (t=2108-2113).

Offence is conditional, not scheduled: the Evo Princess only goes to the bridge when a Cannon is already down — "because I had a free cannon on the board, I also knew I could princess the bridge" (t=2066-2073) — and the Rocket is spent on defence when the hand would otherwise jam (t=2081.6, on a Giant Skeleton).

The failure mode is the same as the deck's strength: with one Rocket and no reset button, a declined Rocket (t=2196-2207) plus a misplaced Cannon (t=2217) let a Mother Witch and Elite Barbarians live, and the towers went from healthy to 363/1009 HP with the king at 266 by t=2248 — "I actually lost because of that, man".

new_deck.rationale: A 2.6-elixir eight-card list with no troop win condition: Rocket and a bridge Evo Princess are the only damage, and every other slot (Evo Cannon, Berserker Hero, Ice Spirit, Skeletons, The Log, Royal Delivery) exists to defend cheaply and cycle back to them.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Everything in the list is 1-3 elixir except the Rocket, so the deck can answer a bridge-spam opponent's threats one at a time and still be back at the Cannon before the next one arrives. The Evo Cannon is placed reactively and centrally to pull Battle Rams and line up on Mother Witches, with Ice Spirit, Skeletons and Berserker layered on top of it; the Berserker Hero's Savage Survival turns a 2-elixir troop into a Giant Skeleton block for a few seconds. Damage comes from an Evo Princess dropped at the bridge only when a Cannon is already banked, plus a Rocket that is as often spent on defence as on a tower. The trade-off is that the deck has exactly one heavy answer: hold the Rocket a beat too long, or misplace the Cannon, and a bridge-spam push with a Mother Witch behind it becomes unanswerable.
